study.title: Locating X-Ray Coronary Angiogram Keyframes via Long Short-Term Spatiotemporal Attention With Image-to-Patch Contrastive Learning

data_released.detail: New XCA video dataset collected from Renji Hospital; release not stated

task.task_description: Locating start, apex and end keyframes of contrast filling/disappearing phases in XCA sequences, formulated as temporal action localization.
task.clinical_application: Keyframe counting of contrast diffusion time span for evaluating coronary microvascular function

architecture_names: STA-IPCon (long short-term spatiotemporal attention with image-to-patch contrastive learning)

temporal_evidence.quote: we propose long short-term spatiotemporal attention by integrating a convolutional long short-term memory (CLSTM) network into a multiscale Transformer

method.class_imbalance_handling: Focal loss for action classification; patchwise contrastive module for foreground/background imbalance

G3.quote: existing methods will ignore a gradually evolving trend of blood vessels in XCA sequence and lead to a loss of long-term dependencies in TAL

G5.quote: supervised learning is tedious and costly in manually annotating the frame- or shot-level labels for video sequences

G7.quote: To improve the explainability of the proposed modules, attention maps are used to show the proposed modules' performance

G9.quote: To solve class-imbalance and imperceptible differences between foreground vessels and vessel-like background disturbances

other_limitations: Predicted start frame may be later than apex frame, affecting P/R/F metrics
Larger deviation on samples with strongly boundary-agnostic characteristics
Actionformer-based regression handles overlapping actions poorly
Attention map artifacts from SVS-Net frame compression
future_work: More principled handling of start/apex frame ordering in evaluation
Application to other flow-like spatiotemporal monitoring scenarios (crowd gathering, traffic inflow/outflow)
